title: Measuring Cilium Length Using 3D Confocal Fluorescence Microscopy
author: Burgdorf, Yüksel, et al.
materials: Visual inspection of the segmentation quality is crucial to further ensure high-precision measurements.CRITICAL: Before proceeding, ensure high quality segmentation by visually inspecting if the ciliary masks fit the signal of the cilia with a high quality. The precision of all measurements depends on the segmentation quality.Note: We recommend choosing a segmentation method that minimizes artifacts. While CiliaQ Editor enables precise adjustments of ciliary masks, removing artifacts using CiliaQ Editor can be time-consuming.13.Analyze the prepared masks using CiliaQ.a.Set the CiliaQ parameters.i.Select “multiple images (open multitask manager)” to include multiple images into the analysis via a file dialog.ii.Select “output number format” to “US (0.00)”.Note: Similar to step 11, CiliaQ can reproduce the analysis by reading the preferences from a previous CiliaQ output file (CQ.txt). If favored, select “Preferences”: “Load Preferences from existing results file (“…CQ.txt”)”Note: CiliaQ is also capable of quantifying signal from additional channel within the ciliary masks (“Channel A″,”Channel B″). This feature is valuable when additional target proteins are included in immunostaining and imaging, enabling quantifying protein localization to the cilium.iii.Under “channels” > “reconstruction”, insert the channel-ID of the ciliary channel in the image that was generated in step 11 and 12 (…CQP.tif).Note: If the data does not contain signal in channel A or B, we recommend keeping the default setting for Channel A/B in step 13a.iii.iv.Set the minimum cilium size depending on your resolution. For lower resolutions of 0.1 μm/px, use 10 voxels (default) and for higher resolutions of e.g., 0.0527 μm/px, use 70 voxels.Note: Consider that pixel size is a length and cilium size an area, which is why if you decrease the pixel size you should increase the minimum cilium size exponentially (1/2 of the pixel size = use a minimum cilium size multiplied by at least 2ˆ2 = 4),Note: The minimum cilium size depends on the magnification used during image acquisition. The indicated size determines the minimum size of an object in your segmented channel that you consider a cilium – if you have non-ciliary objects in the segmented channel that are smaller than the cilia you can gauge their size in pixel and adjust this threshold, so they are removed. For lower magnifications, make sure to use a lower minimum cilium size.v.Select “Increase range for connecting cilia” and “Determine skeleton-based results (e.g., length)” and additionally exclude “cilia touching x or y or z borders”.vi.Introduce a gentle Gaussian Blur on XY-dimensions of the image before skeletonization. Set “gauss filter XY” and sigma to, e.g., 0.

steps.title: Coat glass coverslips
steps.instruction: Insert a 13 mm glass coverslip into a 4‑well or 24‑well plate (well diameter 15.6 mm). Add 500 µL of 1× Poly‑L‑lysine (0.01 % w/v in sterile H₂O) to fully submerge the coverslip, gently push it to the bottom, and incubate 30 min at 21‑23 °C. Remove the PLL solution, wash once with 400 µL 1× PBS, and discard as much PBS as possible. Store sterile 1× PLL at 4 °C (short‑term) or −20 °C (long‑term, up to 18 months) avoiding freeze‑thaw cycles and light exposure.

steps.title: Seed cells on coated coverslips
steps.instruction: Add 100 000 mIMCD‑3 cells in 500 µL sterile DMEM complete medium supplemented with 10 % FCS to each PLL‑coated coverslip. Incubate 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to allow attachment. Do not let the PBS‑washed coverslips dry before seeding.

steps.title: Serum‑starve cells
steps.instruction: Replace the medium in each well with 200 µL starvation medium (DMEM complete without FCS) to promote ciliation. Incubate 12‑16 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Install Fiji and CiliaQ
steps.instruction: Download the Fiji version for your OS from https://imagej.net/software/fiji/downloads, open the executable, go to Help → Update, select “3D Image Suite” and “CiliaQ” under Manage Update Sites, apply changes, and restart Fiji. CiliaQ Preparator v0.1.2 and CiliaQ Editor will then be available under Plugins → CiliaQ.

steps.title: Prepare raw microscopy files
steps.instruction: Open the raw microscopy file, save it as a .tif (File → Save As → Tiff). Create a Maximum Intensity Projection of all slices (Image → Stacks → Z‑Project, Projection Type = Max Intensity). Split the projection into separate channels (Image → Color → Split Channels). Duplicate the ciliary marker channel (Image → Duplicate) and keep the duplicate as a backup.

substeps.instruction: If needed, reduce background: Process → Subtract Background, choose a radius, note the value, and Apply.
If the signal is noisy, smooth with Process → Filters → Gaussian Blur, choose a radius, note the value, and Apply.
Threshold the duplicated marker channel (Image → Adjust → Threshold), select a thresholding algorithm, preview, and Apply.
Convert the image to 8‑bit depth (Image → Type → 8‑bit).
Overlay the binary mask with the duplicated marker (Image → Color → Merge Channels).
Display the merged image as a Composite (Image → Color → Channels Tool) to inspect segmentation quality.

steps.title: Select consistent threshold
steps.instruction: Choose one thresholding algorithm that gives satisfactory ciliary masks and apply it consistently to all images in the dataset. For datasets > 6 images, test the algorithm on representative extreme‑quality images (highest and lowest signal‑to‑noise). Record the chosen algorithm and any radius values used for background subtraction or Gaussian blur.

steps.title: Segment images with CiliaQ Preparator
steps.instruction: Open CiliaQ Preparator (Plugins → CiliaQ → CiliaQ Preparator v0.1.2). Choose processing mode “multiple images (open multi‑task manager)”. Set the channel number of the ciliary marker (≥ 1). Enter the segmentation settings that worked in step 5 (e.g., background subtraction radius, Gaussian blur radius, threshold algorithm). Click OK to run the segmentation on all selected files.

steps.title: Edit masks with CiliaQ Editor
steps.instruction: Launch CiliaQ Editor (Plugins → CiliaQ → CiliaQ Editor). Specify the channel numbers for the segmented mask and the original marker. Use the freehand selection tool to draw regions of interest: press F1 to add a selection to the mask or F2 to remove it. When editing is complete, press “finish analysis and save editings”.

steps.title: Analyze masks with CiliaQ
steps.instruction: Open CiliaQ (Plugins → CiliaQ → CiliaQ). Select “multiple images (open multitask manager)”. Set output number format to US (0.00). Optionally load preferences from an existing CQ.txt file. Under Channels → Reconstruction, enter the channel ID of the ciliary channel generated in steps 7‑8. Set the minimum cilium size: 10 voxels for 0.1 µm/px resolution or 70 voxels for 0.0527 µm/px resolution. Enable “Increase range for connecting cilia”, “Determine skeleton‑based results (e.g., length)”, and exclude cilia touching x, y, or z borders. Apply a gentle Gaussian blur on XY with sigma = 0.5 before skeletonization. Load the _CQP.tif (or _CQPed.tif if edited) files and click “start processing”. Do not close Fiji during analysis.

steps.title: Set up CiliaQ Explorer environment
steps.instruction: Download and install Visual Studio Code (VS Code) from https://code.visualstudio.com/download. Install Python 3.12.4 from https://www.python.org/downloads/ and ensure “Add Python to PATH” is selected. In VS Code, install the Python and Jupyter extensions. Open the CiliaQ Explorer folder (File → Open Folder). Open the Command Palette, run “Python: Create Environment”, choose “Venv”, select the installed Python interpreter, and create the virtual environment. Install the required packages by running `pip install -r requirements.txt` in the terminal. Select the newly created .venv kernel for the notebook.

steps.title: Organize CiliaQ data by condition
steps.instruction: For each experimental condition (group), create a dedicated folder on your computer and copy all CiliaQ‑derived output files (e.g., _CQP.tif, _CQPed.tif, measurement tables) from each replicate into that folder. Use concise, descriptive folder names as they will appear in the final plots.

steps.title: Run CiliaQ Explorer analysis
steps.instruction: Open the CiliaQ Explorer Jupyter notebook in VS Code and run all cells (Run All). In the “Open Directories” dialog, select all group folders created in step 10 and click Apply. In the setup window, click “Select measurements” and choose “Select all” (or a subset). Optionally upload a metafile (Table S1) to provide experimental metadata. Choose whether to compute statistics and set the desired output file format. Confirm the quality‑control dialog. The notebook will generate plots (PNG and SVG) and statistical summaries, saved in the first group folder.

description: Cilia are microscopic, microtubule-based organelles that extend from the cell surface and whose membrane is continuous with the plasma membrane. Fluorescence microscopy is the gold standard method to analyze ciliary morphology and behavior.2,3 Since cilia are oriented in space, performing three-dimensional (3D) analysis of fluorescent images is recommended to retrieve accurate measurements (Figure 1). The Fiji/ImageJ4 plugin CiliaQ1 has been established as a leading tool to segment and measure cilia in 2D-4D fluorescence microscopy images due to its reliable and reproducible outputs. In this protocol, we describe the steps required to label and image cilia of mIMCD-3 cells using a confocal microscope. Of note, due to the high versatility of CiliaQ, the presented procedure can be applied to other microscopy images. This protocol presents results obtained from segmenting cilia based on antibody labeling against Arl13b. Nevertheless, we successfully used CiliaQ to analyze images with different ciliary markers, including acetylated or glutamylated α-tubulin. In addition to ciliary length, all 54 ciliary output parameters from CiliaQ can be analyzed following this protocol, without substantial changes to the workflow. While this protocol describes the analysis of cilia in mIMCD-3 cells, it can be applied to different ciliated cell types, including primary cells, immortalized cell lines, or whole-tissue samples.Figure 1Benefits from performing ciliary analysis on 3-dimensional imagesPerforming ciliary analysis on 2-dimensional images yields a substantial loss of information and leads to inaccurate measurements. When retrieving ciliary information from microscopic images, it is recommended to image a z-stack, consisting of multiple confocal planes. Right: When analyzing only single confocal slice, ciliary signal emerging out of the focal plane is neglected from the analysis, leading to an incomplete mask and thus inaccurate measurements.
